problem: The "average accessibility score" quoted in summary.management_risks[].rationale (build_management_risks, src/output/json/helpers.rs) is computed by average_accessibility_score() (src/output/json/helpers.rs:449) using integer-truncating division (sum / len), which can disagree with summary.accessibility_score's own rounded value for the same nominal statistic when averaging across multiple pages.
evidence: Found by the report-critic skill's dry-run eval against reports/casoon-batch-en301549.json: management_risks[1].rationale literally quoted "84" as the average accessibility score while summary.accessibility_score = 85 (85 = round(); 84 = truncating integer division of the same underlying per-page scores) — the JSON PDF text independently computes and shows 85 correctly, so only the raw JSON field is affected. Confirmed not observable for report_type="single" (average of one value can't diverge from truncation); requires a batch/sitemap report with >=2 pages to reproduce.
expected: Any two fields both claiming to be "the average accessibility score" must use the same rounding rule so they can never silently disagree.
counter_examples: A management_risks rationale for a single-report (exactly one page) is unaffected and must not be flagged, since averaging one value can never diverge under truncation vs. rounding.
